title: Liquid Biopsy Biomarkers in Metastatic Prostate Cancer: A Multicenter Observational Study Protocol
author: Michalski, Kerstin
materials: Treatment response is further assessed by analyzing longitudinal changes in ctDNA levels and their concordance with PSMA PET-CT and PSA responses, using the Cohen κ coefficient and correlation analyses. Secondary analyses investigate associations between baseline and longitudinal ctDNA metrics and clinical or laboratory parameters, including subgroup comparisons based on patient characteristics. Exploratory analyses focus on the identification of very early molecular responders based on short-term ctDNA changes and on the characterization of clonal evolution and potential resistance mechanisms using deep sequencing and computational clonal deconvolution methods. General statistical considerations include the handling of missing data, adjustment for multiple testing, and sensitivity analyses to ensure robustness of the results. Given that tumor burden and ctDNA levels may change over relatively short time intervals in heavily pretreated mCRPC, the temporal separation between baseline PSMA PET-CT imaging and baseline blood sampling will be accounted for in the statistical analysis. The exact interval (in days) between PET-CT and blood draw will be recorded for all patients. The primary analysis correlating baseline ctDNA with PET-derived tumor burden will be prespecified to include only patients with a PET-to-blood interval of ≤28 days. In addition, sensitivity analyses will be performed in the full cohort, incorporating the PET-to-blood interval as a covariate (modeled as a continuous variable and as a categorical variable ≤28 vs 29‐56 days). Patients with intervals exceeding 28 days will be described separately, and the impact of their inclusion vs exclusion on key estimates will be explicitly reported. Furthermore, we will assess the association between cumulative administered activity and longitudinal changes of ctDNA. Cumulative activity will be modeled as a continuous exposure variable and analyzed in relation to ctDNA dynamics using regression-based approaches. Landmark analyses will be used where appropriate to mitigate immortal time bias.

steps.title: Identify eligible patients and obtain consent
steps.instruction: Screen adults (≥18 y) with histologically confirmed mCRPC who have received ≥1 AR pathway inhibitor and ≥1 taxane, have a PSMA PET‑CT within 8 weeks showing adequate target expression, and meet all inclusion criteria; provide study information during treatment planning and obtain written informed consent (German‑speaking or with translator).

steps.title: Schedule baseline and follow‑up sampling/imaging
steps.instruction: Enroll participants before cycle 1. Plan blood draws at baseline (≤14 days before cycle 1), before cycle 2 (≈6 weeks), and after cycles 2, 4, 6 (≈16, 28, 40 weeks). Include an exploratory draw at 6 weeks after the first cycle for early molecular response. Schedule PSMA PET‑CT at baseline and after cycles 2, 4, 6; ensure baseline PET‑CT is ≤8 weeks before cycle 1 and record the exact PET‑to‑blood interval in days.

steps.title: Collect peripheral blood in EDTA tubes
steps.instruction: At each time point draw peripheral blood into ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA) tubes: 5 × 9 mL tubes at baseline and 3 × 9 mL tubes at every follow‑up visit.

steps.title: Process blood and store plasma
steps.instruction: Within 2 hours of collection, perform a double‑spin centrifugation of each tube, aliquot the plasma into labeled cryovials, and store at –80 °C. Simultaneously isolate matched leukocyte DNA from the cell pellet for later germline/CHIP filtering. Use the standardized SOP adapted from the Augsburg Longitudinal Plasma Study and a barcode‑based chain‑of‑custody system.

steps.title: Extract cell‑free DNA from plasma
steps.instruction: From each plasma sample, take approximately 4 mL and extract cell‑free DNA using the laboratory‑validated kit. Quantify the cfDNA and assess fragment‑size distribution before downstream processing.

steps.title: Prepare sequencing libraries and sequence
steps.instruction: Construct libraries with the AVENIO ctDNA Surveillance V2 panel (197 genes, includes NCCN prostate cancer genes, incorporates unique molecular identifiers for error suppression). Sequence paired‑end 100 bp reads on an Illumina NovaSeq X aiming for >20,000× raw coverage.

steps.title: Perform bioinformatic analysis and compute ΔctDNA
steps.instruction: Run the validated pipeline to call single‑nucleotide variants, indels, and copy‑number alterations; summarize ctDNA burden as variant‑allele fractions and human‑genome‑equivalents. Calculate ΔctDNA as the percent change from the baseline value for each on‑treatment time point. Filter out germline variants and clonal‑hematopoiesis‑associated mutations (e.g., DNMT3A, TET2, ASXL1) using the matched leukocyte DNA data. Apply the pre‑specified quality metrics and reporting thresholds uniformly.

steps.title: Administer [177Lu]Lu‑PSMA‑617 therapy
steps.instruction: Deliver [177Lu]Lu‑PSMA‑617 intravenously every 6 weeks per routine clinical practice, for up to 6 cycles, following the manufacturer’s dosing recommendations. The treating physician may initiate, delay, or discontinue treatment at discretion; no protocol‑specific dosing modifications are made.

steps.title: Perform PSMA PET‑CT imaging
steps.instruction: Acquire PET‑CT scans at baseline and after cycles 2, 4, 6 according to each site’s SOP:

substeps.instruction: Würzburg: Use Siemens Biograph mCT 64 or mCT 128 Flow; inject [¹⁸F]PSMA‑1007 at 3 MBq/kg; scan 90 min post‑injection; whole‑body acquisition 2 min per bed position.
Augsburg: Use Siemens Biograph mCT 40 or GE Discovery Molecular Imaging; inject ~4 MBq/kg of either [¹⁸F]rhPSMA‑7.3 or [¹⁸F]DCFPyL (Pylarify); scan 60 min post‑injection; 2 min per bed position.

Munich (TUM): Use Siemens Biograph molecular CT or Biograph Vision 600; inject 3 MBq/kg [¹⁸F]rhPSMA‑7.3 (or 3 MBq/kg [¹⁸F]PSMA‑1007 during cyclotron maintenance); scan 60 min after [rhPSMA‑7.3] or 90 min after [PSMA‑1007]; acquisition 3–4 min per bed position or flow speed 1.1–1.5 mm/s.
Follow‑up scans: Tracer may differ from baseline depending on local availability; record any change.

steps.title: Pseudonymize and centrally review PET‑CT images
steps.instruction: Pseudonymize all DICOM images and transfer them to the central review site (Würzburg). Perform visual response assessment using RECIP 1.0 relative to baseline after cycles 2, 4, 6. Use a single reader; if the radiotracer changed between scans, have two readers reach consensus. Document the number of patients with tracer changes.

steps.title: Capture and store clinical and laboratory data
steps.instruction: Prospectively record demographics, baseline tumor characteristics (Gleason score, metastatic sites), laboratory values (PSA, lactate dehydrogenase, alkaline phosphatase), and treatment details (administered cycles and activity). Pseudonymize the dataset and upload to the central electronic data capture master file at University Hospital Würzburg. Also record the PET‑to‑blood interval (in days) for each patient; flag intervals ≤28 days for primary analyses.

steps.title: Archive source documents and biospecimens
steps.instruction: Retain all original clinical source documents at the treating hospitals for a minimum of 30 years (radiation protection ordinance). Archive liquid‑biopsy results for 30 years at the Interdisciplinary Laboratory for Experimental Cancer Research. Store pseudonymized PET‑CT DICOM data together with clinical data for 10 years. Ensure all biospecimens are barcoded, stored under controlled conditions, and shipped according to applicable regulations.
